request: User explicitly requires SQL-only recovery, without a filesystem journal.
scope: Map character/item persistence and QuestEngine/mail continuation recovery. Native gameplay tables remain the persistent game state.
implemented: Removed the filesystem SaveJournal implementation. SqlSaveQueue commits immutable save entries into dbo.TCharacterSaveQueue before dirty flags or pending item operations are cleared. No file writes, directory identity, file lease or filesystem fallback exists in this path.

Migration 043 creates TCharacterSaveOwner and TCharacterSaveQueue. Owner/database identity and a session-owned SQL application lock protect each queue domain. The default owner is group-server; SaveQueueName is an optional SQL scope, not a path. Owner keys use binary collation and trimmed input to keep SQL identity and lock naming consistent.

Queue payloads are checksummed JSON text INSIDE SQL, preserving tuple fields, full item attributes, native character/auxiliary snapshots and version-2 quest-mail intents/receipts. Native SQL fields remain in their original game tables. Successful application deletes the queued SQL row; failed or interrupted work remains in SQL for ordered replay.

Normal quest acceptance/turn-in and mail checkpoints combine pending item operations and the full snapshot in ONE SQL queue commit. Direct operations apply before the full inventory state in the existing single DB lane. A rejected queue insertion cannot persist only a starter/reward item; failure quarantines the session and prevents item/logout/map-leave leakage.

Startup and login drain SQL work before exposing a character. SendPost still atomically reserves attachments/progress/outbox events in TQuestPostOperation; nested and sibling mail have stable issuance IDs and receipts. Character/mail continuations run at CS_CONREADY and acknowledge only after replayable SQL stages succeed.

The SQL lease disables pooling and automatic reconnect. A missing queue schema, wrong database identity, corrupt record, competing owner or lost lease fails closed. SQL outages have no local persistence fallback. Previously confirmed SQL rows survive a worker crash; an unconfirmed action cannot be promised durable when SQL cannot accept it.

Removed Map:SaveJournalDirectory, the compose Map__SaveJournalDirectory override and the map-state save volume/mount. Existing SQL data volumes remain. This changes configuration only; no Docker volume or production player data was deleted.

history_review.reason: The user chose SQL-only recovery. Durable queue acceptance now uses a synchronous SQL commit at the actor's existing durability boundary; applying native gameplay table changes remains asynchronous on the preserved DB lane. This avoids changing every synchronous quest/item entry point while keeping acknowledgements after durable acceptance. No Gameforge content, balance or quest rules were added.

remaining: Native character/global/item/pet/companion application still comprises multiple SQL transactions. The SQL queue makes ordered replay durable; it does not turn all stages into one atomic gameplay transaction.

External world-effect mail children (teleport, switches, spawns, monster death/regen/corpse drops) remain explicitly pending/blocked until a durable world-effect protocol exists. Cross-Map character-owner fencing/routing remains incomplete; the queue lease is not universal distributed character ownership.
RT_SOUL and TT_WARREGION reference contracts remain unresolved. Full real-client journeys and actual MapWorker shutdown/restart with this build remain acceptance gates.

Migrations 041 through 046 and current Map/World source are deployed (Gameforge/deployments/2026-10-30-wolverine.json). The earlier filesystem implementation was never deployed; no production file queue was imported or discarded. Old ignored test artifacts are historical evidence, not runtime state.

Back up queued rows and TQuestPostOperation with the matching game/global databases. SQL lease loss requires a fresh worker ownership session; the old owner does not reconnect and resume writes automatically.
